findings.evidence: Kauffman.lean:103-108 `def slotSmoothing (b : Bool) := if b then Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 2 3 else ...` with `slotSmoothing_true ... := (rfl)`; Kauffman.lean:116 `slotSmoothing_apply_apply (b) (slot) : slotSmoothing b (slotSmoothing b slot) = slot`; Kauffman.lean:122 `slotSmoothing_ne (b) (slot) : slotSmoothing b slot ≠ slot`. These match `PerfectMatching.mk (f) (hinv : ∀ a, f (f a) = a) (hne : ∀ a, f a ≠ a)` (PerfectMatching.lean:103) argument for argument.
findings.fix: Move `slotSmoothing` and `slotSmoothing_true`/`slotSmoothing_false`/`slotSmoothing_apply_apply`/`slotSmoothing_ne` from Kauffman.lean into Basic.lean next to `oppositeCrossingSlot` (Basic.lean:120 — they use nothing from Kauffman and need no new import), then write `edgePair := PerfectMatching.mk (slotSmoothing true) (slotSmoothing_apply_apply true) (slotSmoothing_ne true)` and state `kink_edgePair_val` as `kink.edgePair.val = slotSmoothing true`. Alternatively leave `kink` in Kauffman.lean and move `positiveKink` there, which also removes the duplicate definition.
findings.issue: `edgePair := PerfectMatching.mk (Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 2 3) (by intro h; fin_cases h <;> simp [Equiv.swap_apply_def]) (by intro h; fin_cases h <;> simp [Equiv.swap_apply_def])` re-spells `slotSmoothing true` and re-proves its involutivity and fixed-point-freeness, all three of which already exist. The deleted Kauffman version used the combinator.

findings.evidence: Kauffman.lean:417-420 `have hc (s : Fin 4) : crossingSlotEquiv 1 (i, s) = s := ...; rw [kink_edgePair_val, hc, hc]; fin_cases t <;> decide`, replacing the deleted `simp [kink, PerfectMatching.congr_val, PerfectMatching.val_mk]` shown in the diff.
findings.fix: With `slotSmoothing` available in Basic and `kink.edgePair := PerfectMatching.mk (slotSmoothing true) ...`, this reverts to the one-line proof; no `hc` and no `fin_cases` needed.
findings.issue: Same root cause: `kink_edgePair_apply` was definitional (`simp [kink, PerfectMatching.congr_val, PerfectMatching.val_mk]`) because the arcs *were* `slotSmoothing true` transported by `crossingSlotEquiv`. It is now re-derived by a local `hc` plus `fin_cases t <;> decide`, i.e. a case bash recovering what the old definition gave for free.

summary: The PR does remove the real duplication: PDCode.kink now has a single definition and positiveKink is built on it. But moving kink upstream of slotSmoothing forces the matching and both of its PerfectMatching.mk obligations to be re-spelled from raw swaps, re-deriving slotSmoothing true, slotSmoothing_apply_apply and slotSmoothing_ne.
